summary.text: A 27-year-old man, a healthcare provider and nonsmoker with one previous arrhythmic episode in 2018 linked to alcohol with nausea and vomiting, presented in December 2020 to the Emergency Department with a recurrence of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response after a nasopharyngeal swab for SARS-CoV-2. He had rapid irregular palpitations, and the onset followed a transient sinus bradycardia during sampling.

An Apple Watch ECG suggested atrial fibrillation and a standard 12-lead ECG confirmed AF with rapid ventricular response of 150-170 bpm. He was hospitalized for rhythm control. Examination, admission laboratory tests, bedside echocardiography and risk scores showed a CHA2DS2-VASc score of 0, and valvular or structural alterations were excluded; reflux disease, hypertension, diabetes and hyperthyroidism were ruled out.

No anticoagulation was initiated; intravenous propafenone was given for pharmacological cardioversion, and stable sinus rhythm was restored and maintained during the hospitalization. After a next-day echocardiogram he was discharged home with optional edoxaban. A cardiac MRI one month later showed no abnormalities, and over one year of follow-up no AF recurrence was shown or reported.

article_limitations: Caption-layer visual status is not_inspected; the five figure JPEGs were inspected in the separate visual submission.

Supplementary Figure S1 (Apple Health screenshots in a one-page PDF inside a ZIP) carries printed values and date and time stamps in pixels; its values are not extracted as facts, and the caption-only text mention of sinus bradycardia has no printed value in the article text.

Table 1 values are recorded with their printed reference ranges and no flag from those ranges; the narrative statement that panels were within reference ranges conflicts arithmetically with several printed rows and is kept review_only.
